newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate jumps to 10.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate jumps to 10.7 pct.

text.p: Interbank borrowing at higher rates boosted the Croatian money market rate to 10.7 percent from 8.7 percent in brisker trade on Friday.
Dealers said demand was completely satisfied, and total settlements rose to 30.5 million kuna against the suply of 35 million.
New borrowings were made at a higher rate of 9.0 percent for call money and 15.3 percent for longer-term loans. A smaller 11-15 day loan was struck at 9.7 percent.
Insurers rolled over previous loans at a steady 8.0 percent rate.
Overnight trade totalled 42 million kuna, of which banks used 30 million to maintain their mandatory reserve. Another 12 million kuna were granted to two banks with shortfalls.
The central bank its kuna midrates for the weekend and next Monday firmer at 5.4396 against the dollar and 3.5562 against the German mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-45575
